question.prompt: The numeral \(47\) in base \(a\) represents the same number as \(74\) in base \(b.\) Assuming both bases are positive integers, the least possible value of \(a+b,\) written as a Roman numeral, is:

solutions.explanation:
A base must be larger than every digit used in its numerals. Since both numerals contain the digit \(7\), we need \(a\ge8\) and \(b\ge8\).

Using place value, the equality of the two numerals becomes
\[4a+7=7b+4,\qquad a=\frac{7b-3}{4}.\]
If \(b=8\), this gives \(a=\frac{53}{4}\), which is not an integer. The next possibility, \(b=9\), gives \(a=15\), an allowed base. Indeed,
\[4(15)+7=67=7(9)+4.\]
To check minimality, observe that
\[a+b=\frac{11b-3}{4}\]
increases as \(b\) increases. We have ruled out the only smaller allowed value of \(b\), so \(15+9=24\) is the least sum.

In Roman numerals, \(20=\mathrm{XX}\) and \(4=\mathrm{IV}\), giving \(\boxed{\mathrm{XXIV}}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
solutions.title: Test the smallest possible bases
